title: Has anyone had any luck with LLM-generated Blender scripts?
author: Mental_Wealth1491
selftext:
I’ve been experimenting with having Claude and ChatGPT write Blender scripts to create meshes for various objects, mostly buildings and other similar infrastructure. The two biggest issues I’ve ran into are the following:

  
1. They generally create ultra low-poly meshes by default and you have to constantly reprompt the model to remind it that you want the actual shape of the requested object, not 2-5 rectangular prisms slapped together.

  
2. Anything with lots of precise curves (such as cars or faces) ends up looking like incomprehensible garbage.

  
I’m particularly interested in responses from people who have tried this, noticed some of the same issues, and developed a less naive approach that yielded better results.

comments.author: Recoil42
comments.body: You won't get good output with the current language models, which don't really have good spatial comprehension. Use a model generator like Tripo.

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body:
I do use LLMs but for shaders and tools instead of models, for models I use Gaussian Splatting.

You can make your own AI to make models, but an LLM will not help you do it. I think they are designed to avoid helping you make your own LLM models. Instead you can look up how to make them from scratch, and ask the LLM to teach you the math. - The down side is the models they make aren't as good as Gaussian Splatting, all modern 3D AI generators use Gaussian Splatting or Point Clouds (photogrammetry style).

comments.author: SquirrelTomahawk
comments.body: Why use Blender when Hunyan 3D exist for pennies

replies.author: Mental_Wealth1491
replies.body: Nice. What types of assets are you building with it and what have you learned since you started doing it?

comments.author: CordusPorf
comments.body: Yes. With codex,  I'm able to have it run python code on my active blender session,  using the blender API it can do anything you can do from the UI and more.  For example,  I've had it build excellent procedural materials.

comments.author: saulplastik
comments.body:
I use this for image > 3D: [https://github.com/TencentARC/Pixal3D](https://github.com/TencentARC/Pixal3D)

very good. I use it as a base that i can use to measure proportions while i build a better cleaner mesh right next to it.

comments.author: Former_Currency_3474
comments.body:
Create meshes? No, horrible. But as far as doing anything else, like complex systemic tasks, it’s absolutely great. 

Actually I’ve been using Claude to make a bunch of complex linear algebra geometry node groups and it has been killing it.
